Yay! Another Chinese SCP! Definitely connected to Emperor ShiHuangDi, which bring up the argument that it could have belonged to him, which makes it more interesting! I also found it funny that, coincidence or not, SCP-926's Shaanxi and the terra-cotta warriors' Xian have reversed names. I agree that the many note combinations make it quite an interesting thing to be experimented, but that could add to your story, perhaps if there were more destructive ways to use it. Putting it into the wrong hands could change its class! I dunno. Just some story fuel ;)

好棒好棒！

Still, this is great. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really quite like this. It's fairly simple, but effective in "How many of these things ARE there?!" and "What the hell else was going on in Ancient China we don't know about?!".

It's lovely to see a Chinese artifact SCP. There's such a rich history to be drawn from, both in scope and scale of myths, that it's surprising there are so few in the roster.

While not overly familiar with Chinese music, I must applaud the detail you put into the testing log. That really made it for me.

Upvoted with pleasure and looking forward to more.
